subject: Payload transfer & traffic dry-run — scheduling and redaction checklist
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightlane.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightlane Eng <eng@brightlane.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: move Oct 1 hands-on + payload transfer before session

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Quick ask from our side — an exec conflict just came up and we need to move the Oct 1 hands-on working session to later in the week if possible (preferably Oct 5). We still want the same agenda: 90 minutes of prompt routing + routing policy review, followed by a 30–45 min traffic dry-run to verify routing and load behavior.

Before we lock the new time, can you confirm:
- availability on Oct 5 between 10:00–13:00 PT?
- whether Redwood can run a dry-run at ~150–200 RPS for a 15-minute window (we'll throttle from our side too)?
- a redaction checklist we should apply to the sample payloads we upload (we will not send PHI but want to be sure)

I can upload a small set of representative payloads to the Drive link below once we confirm — these will be sanitized but are realistic. Also cc'ing our engineering alias so the load/ingest team can chime in.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_sample_payloads

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Product Integrations, Brightlane Health
ellen.park@brightlane.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Note: attached earlier drafts were internal; we'll only share sanitized samples.
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: move Oct 1 hands-on + payload transfer before session

Ellen — thanks for the heads up. Oct 5 10:00–13:00 PT works on our side; we can split it as 10:00–11:30 prompt/review + 11:45–12:30 dry-run + 12:30–13:00 wrap (notes/action items).

We can run the dry-run at 200 RPS sustained for a 15-minute window provided we agree on the payload size distribution in advance (avg token size, typical prompt/response lengths). A couple small logistics asks from our side:

- Please upload a CSV of up to 5k rows (sample_payloads.csv) to the Drive folder. Include columns: id, prompt, expected_top_intent (optional), redaction_flag.
- Run our redaction checklist before upload — I attached the checklist we use as a PDF (samples_redaction_checklist.pdf). It lists fields to remove or mask and sample regexes we recommend.
- For the dry-run we will: warm KV cache using the first 1k prompts, run a 15-min steady-state at the target RPS, and stream logs to a temporary trace (we'll share link).
- Please let us know if you want token-level tracing or anonymized latency histograms only. Token tracing requires a signed DPA amendment; histograms do not.

I attached the redaction checklist. If that's okay, upload the sample CSV and a short eval subset (eval_prompts_subset.jsonl) so we can run a quick quality check before the session.

If you confirm the time I'll send a calendar invite with required dial-in and runbook links.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
(650) 555-0148

Attachments: samples_redaction_checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightlane.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: move Oct 1 hands-on + payload transfer before session

Ellen — thanks. Confirming the Oct 5 window works for me too. I've included Ben to own the dry-run config and the traffic shaping on our side.

Quick notes for the agenda and what we'll prepare:
- 10:00–11:30: prompt review and routing policy mapping (we'll walk through routing rules, fallbacks, and function/tool calling examples).
- 11:45–12:30: traffic dry-run (Ben will start the warmup at 11:40; warmup plan below).
- 12:30–13:00: results, immediate action items, and next steps.

Warmup plan (Ben):
- Phase 1 (0–5min): sequential warmup of 1k unique prefixes to populate KV caches.
- Phase 2 (5–10min): ramp from 10 RPS to 80% of target.
- Phase 3 (10–15min): sustain at 200 RPS for 15 min window (steady-state), collect token-latency histograms.

Routing & prompt notes:
- Please flag any prompts that require deterministic routing (i.e., exact-match intents) in the redaction_flag column.
- For heterogeneous lengths, include token_count as an optional column — we use it to tune batching/sequence packing.

Ben (cc) — can you confirm you'll provide the temporary trace link and the runbook embed?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
